questions.question: In a digraph, a can reach b, and b can reach c. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: a, b and c are strongly connected
questions.explanation: Reachability is transitive, because you can join the two walks end to end. It is not symmetric, so nothing lets you travel back against the arrows.

questions.question: Why is the condensation graph of any digraph acyclic?
options: Because every digraph is a DAG
Because each SCC has only one vertex
Because a cycle through several SCCs would make them mutually reachable, so they would be one SCC
questions.explanation: SCCs are maximal sets of mutually reachable vertices. A cycle between components would merge them, which contradicts their maximality.

questions.question: In the proof that every DAG has a topological order, why remove a source and not some other vertex?
options: A source has nothing that must come before it, so it can safely be listed first
Sources have the most outgoing arrows
Removing a source makes the graph strongly connected
Only sources can be removed without deleting edges
questions.explanation: Placing the source first breaks no constraint, since no vertex reaches it. Induction then orders the smaller DAG that remains.

questions.question: A project DAG has 30 tasks, and its longest dependency chain has 7 tasks. With unlimited workers, what is the fastest finish?
options: It depends on which topological order you pick
questions.explanation: The minimum span equals the number of vertices on a longest path, which is 7 here. Scheduling each task at its depth achieves it.
